facebook.long_form:
Victor Wembanyama reminded the world last night why he's the most exciting player on earth — and he did it in front of a crowd that couldn't believe what it was seeing.

Playing in Stockholm's Avicii Arena in a FIBA World Cup 2027 qualifier, Wemby dropped 18 points, 8 rebounds, 3 blocks and a steal while shooting an almost-perfect 6-of-7 from the field. France was trailing Sweden 65-64 with just five minutes left. Then Wembanyama took over, and the game wasn't close anymore — final score: France 84, Sweden 69.

The crowd? 14,750 fans packed into that arena — the single largest audience ever to watch a basketball game on Swedish soil. When Wemby locked in, even the home fans couldn't help but watch in awe.

France improves to 7-1 in Group L — the undisputed top spot — and they're marching toward 2027 World Cup qualification. For the Spurs faithful, this is must-watch basketball. This is your franchise cornerstone on the international stage, and he's delivering every single time.

The fourth quarter belongs to Wemby.

facebook.long_form:
The Kawhi Leonard saga is entering what could be its final chapter — and the NBA Board of Governors meeting this September is the moment everyone has been waiting for.

Here's where things stand: The Raptors and Clippers agreed to a blockbuster trade on June 30. Kawhi goes to Toronto; Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round picks, and a swap head to LA. It seemed done. Then, on July 9, Toronto hit pause — the NBA's ongoing investigation into Kawhi's Clippers contract had created uncertainty about potential sanctions that could affect the Raptors.

Eleven months of investigation later (led by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz), Kawhi Leonard has been personally cleared. The Clippers are still facing potential sanctions. And Kawhi himself? Per reports, he strongly believes this trade is getting done before training camp begins on September 28 in Quebec City.

The BOG meeting this month is described as the key inflection point — where sanctions get handed down and the trade gets the green light. If it happens, Toronto gets their cornerstone back. If it doesn't, the league enters camp with one of its biggest stars in limbo.

All eyes on September.

Final rosters are being locked in. The 2026-27 season is coming. 🏀 #NBA

facebook.long_form:
Twenty-nine days. That's all that stands between now and NBA training camp — and rosters are still shifting.

The latest: Bennedict Mathurin is officially an unrestricted free agent. The Los Angeles Clippers withdrew his qualifying offer on August 29, officially releasing him from any restricted status. Mathurin had previously agreed in principle to a two-year, $16 million deal with the New Orleans Pelicans — one that should now be formalized.

Meanwhile, John Konchar was waived by the Minnesota Timberwolves through the stretch provision on August 30, clearing cap space as the Wolves finalize their roster around Jonathan Kuminga (2yr/$12.43M) and LaMelo Ball.

The final pieces are being locked in. Veterans report September 28. Camps open September 29. Preseason kicks off October 3. And then Opening Night — October 20 on NBC.

The 2026-27 NBA season is almost here. Is your team ready?

facebook.long_form:
The Miami Heat are ready. All 14 roster spots are filled, training camp is 29 days away, and South Beach is about to become the hottest destination in basketball.

Giannis Antetokounmpo arrived in a July 6 blockbuster (Milwaukee received Tyler Herro, Ware, Jaquez, and draft picks). Klay Thompson inked a 2-year, $11.48M deal after his Dallas buyout. Nick Richards added frontcourt depth on a 1-year, $3.06M deal. Two-way players Hadley and Johnson round out the group.

This isn't just a superteam — it's one of the most intriguing rosters assembled in years. Giannis and Bam Adebayo as a twin-tower frontcourt. Klay Thompson's shooting alongside a fully healthy Heat backcourt. The culture Jimmy Butler built — still present in the locker room DNA.

Christmas Day, they host the Celtics. On January 6, 2027, Giannis becomes eligible for a $275M supermax extension. This Heat team isn't just built to compete — it's built to dominate.

The regular season can't get here fast enough.

facebook.long_form:
October 20 cannot arrive fast enough.

The NBA's Opening Night tripleheader on NBC is shaping up to be one of the most anticipated single nights in league history. Here's why:

**Game 1 (3 PM ET):** Boston Celtics at Detroit Pistons — a marquee early matchup that opens the day.

**Game 2 (7 PM ET):** Philadelphia 76ers at New York Knicks — Madison Square Garden, the most iconic arena in basketball, will be electric. LeBron James, Joel Embiid, and Jaylen Brown making their 76ers debut against the defending NBA champions. The Knicks raising their first banner since 1973. A title ceremony. An LeBron rivalry. Everything.

**Game 3 (9:30 PM ET):** Oklahoma City Thunder at San Antonio Spurs — a rematch of last season's Western Conference Finals, with Victor Wembanyama looking for revenge on the team that eliminated the Spurs.

LeBron James called Philadelphia his "last decision." The 76ers' championship odds have moved from 20-1 to 10-1. And the entire country will be tuned in to NBC for the first time in years for an NBA opener.

Fifty days. Mark the calendar.
